page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. This instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V1 CPU model running at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance in single-core operations but reveal limitations in multi-core and memory-intensive tasks. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1532.89 and Geekbench single-core score of 1514.0 both rank in the average tier. Single-threaded data processing tasks also show moderate capability, with gzip compression reaching 24.09 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 9.3 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks fall into the weak or poor categories, as evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 3043.47 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 17.68 GB/sec. Memory performance is also constrained, with a Passmark memory score of 1055.37 and a large-block uncached write speed of 20.86 GB/sec.

The c7gn.large instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from dedicated ARM-based compute resources and high network throughput without requiring extensive memory capacity. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded applications. This is reflected in the weak Passmark database operations score of 2033.45 and static web serving throughput of 4.38 GB/sec. The instance is best suited for lightweight, network-optimized workloads, single-threaded utility tasks, and basic web serving or development environments optimized for the ARM64 architecture.
